Water 'slips' over the slope sometimes down to depths of 600-1000 m and reaches the oxygen minimum layer. Under these conditions renewal of water in the oxygen minimum layer and upwelling of deep water in the adjacent cyclonic eddies take place. The new data call for revision of earlier ideas on the rate of vertical surface, intermediate and deep water exchange.
